why: linux-x1 found their 0.22 ppm closure was not an error bar - two runs closed to ~0.2 each while disagreeing by 1.3 ppm on the absolute arms, because a shift common to both terms cancels in the ratio. I had quoted my 0.18 the same way. This is the repetition the closure cannot provide.
findings: the absolute arms move together and the ratio does not: board range 0.73, host range 0.54, ratio range 0.19. The ratio is TIGHTER than either term it is made of, which is exactly the common-mode cancellation linux-x1 described and is why the closure stayed between 0.11 and 0.37 while the board arm moved 0.73

this bench's reproducibility is BETTER than linux-x1's - board sd 0.33 against their ~0.73 from two runs - which I did not expect, having predicted worse because w32time polls every nine hours against chronyd steering continuously
conclusion: the 4 ppm board separation and the 17 ppm host separation are both far larger than the run-to-run spreads that now bound them, so both are real. The boards are close; the USB host controllers are not.
